# Baruch Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** The Lord our God has done exactly what he said he would do — to us, to the judges who ruled Israel, to our kings and leaders, to every man and woman of Israel and Judah.

**2** He has brought on us disasters greater than anything that has happened under the whole sky, disasters like those that fell on Jerusalem — everything written in the law of Moses has come true,

**3** including the most terrible thing of all: that people would eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters.

**4** He handed us over to all the surrounding kingdoms to be humiliated and laid waste — scattered among all the peoples around us, just as he said he would.

**5** We were brought down and not lifted up, because we sinned against the Lord our God and refused to listen to his voice.

**6** The Lord our God is in the right. We are the ones covered in shame — we and our ancestors — and so it remains to this day.

**7** Every disaster the Lord warned us about has now come upon us.

**8** And still we did not seek the Lord's face or turn from the evil thoughts of our hearts.

**9** The Lord watched as the disasters unfolded and brought them upon us, because he is righteous in everything he does and everything he commands.

**10** But we would not obey him. We would not walk in the ways he had set before us.

**11** O Lord, God of Israel — you who brought your people out of Egypt with a mighty hand, with signs and wonders, with great power and an outstretched arm, making yourself a name that has lasted to this day —

**12** we have sinned against you. We have been wicked. We have done wrong in every way, O Lord our God, against every ordinance you gave us.

**13** Turn your anger away from us. We are only a remnant left scattered among the nations.

**14** Hear our prayer, Lord. Hear our cry. Deliver us, not because we deserve it, but for your own name's sake. Give us favor in the eyes of those who took us captive,

**15** so that the whole world may know that you are the Lord our God, for Israel and her children carry your name.

**16** Look down from your holy dwelling, Lord, and notice us. Lean in and listen.

**17** Open your eyes and see — because the dead in Hades cannot praise you or declare that you are righteous.

**18** But the person crushed by grief, bent low and barely walking, with failing eyes and a soul hollowed out by hunger — that person will give you glory and declare your righteousness, O Lord.

**19** We are not coming to you on the basis of our ancestors' goodness, O Lord our God.

**20** We come because you yourself sent your anger and wrath upon us, exactly as you had warned through your servants the prophets:

**21** "This is what the Lord says: Bow your neck and serve the king of Babylon. Stay in the land I gave your ancestors.

**22** If you refuse to serve the king of Babylon and will not obey me,

**23** I will silence Judah's towns. I will empty Jerusalem's streets of laughter and joy — no more voices of bride and bridegroom, no more celebrations. The whole land will become a wasteland, empty of people."

**24** But we did not listen. We would not serve the king of Babylon. So you kept your word. Everything the prophets had said came true: the bones of our kings and our ancestors were dragged out of their graves.

**25** They were flung out to the blazing sun by day and the bitter cold at night, and they died in agony — by famine, by the sword, by exile.

**26** The temple where your name was honored — you have left it as it stands today, ruined by the wickedness of Israel and Judah.

**27** And yet, O Lord our God, you have treated us according to your own goodness and your great compassion —

**28** just as you told your servant Moses on the day you gave him your law to set before Israel, saying:

**29** "If you will not listen to me, this great multitude will dwindle to nothing among the nations I scatter them to.

**30** I know they will not listen — they are stubborn people. But in the land of their exile, they will finally come to their senses.

**31** They will know that I am the Lord their God. I will give them hearts that understand and ears that hear.

**32** They will praise me from the place of their exile and remember who I am.

**33** They will turn away from their stubbornness and their evil, and they will remember the path their ancestors walked — the path that led to sin.

**34** Then I will bring them home — to the land I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. They will live in it again; I will make them many, not few.

**35** I will make an everlasting covenant with them: I will be their God and they will be my people. And I will never again uproot my people Israel from the land I have given them."

---
*PNEUMA notes: The prayer in this chapter is one of the finest confessional prayers in Jewish literature, parallel to Dan 9 and Neh 9. The movement from shame (vv.1-10) through plea (vv.11-19) to the embedded Mosaic oracle (vv.20-35) is preserved with its full rhetorical arc. v.17 the contrast between the dead who cannot praise and the living sufferer who can is a profound theological moment — rendered with appropriate weight.*
